items.scene: Noah promised to cover the 4 p.m. shift at the bookstore. At 3:45 p.m., his friend texts asking him to join a movie instead.
items.question: What should Noah prioritize?
options: The bookstore shift he already promised to cover
The movie invitation because it is more fun
Whichever option he feels like in the moment
Neither; he should ignore both plans
items.why_this_case_matters: This is a direct priority conflict between an existing commitment and a new invitation.

items.scene: Lena is already helping her neighbor move boxes. While she is carrying a table, her coworker asks if she can come in early for an extra task.
items.question: Which plan has priority right now?
options: The coworker's extra task because it is new
The task she is already doing for her neighbor
The option that sounds most important emotionally
Neither; both should be treated the same
items.why_this_case_matters: An ongoing task already underway should outrank a new request unless an override is stated.

items.scene: Eli wants to finish his report or play a video game after work. No one has promised anything, and no deadline has been set.
items.question: Which unit best fits this scene?
items.why_this_case_matters: This is only a wish-versus-wish choice with no binding commitment structure.

items.scene: Mina promised to help at the community fair, but later she told the organizer she could not come because of a family emergency.
items.question: Why is this a poor match for Commitment Priority?
options: Because there is no prior commitment at all
Because the promise was canceled, so the conflict is no longer active
Because the scene is mainly about what she will do next
Because the scene only describes a mood
items.why_this_case_matters: The earlier promise has already been explicitly overridden, so priority ranking is not the main issue.
